headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Langflow orchestrates OpenMetadata via shared files and MCP/API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write files and chain agents in graph-based flows, while OpenMetadata exposes APIs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Langflow ingests OpenMetadata outputs or shared files as trusted text. The interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Langflow nodes ingest OpenMetadata webhook/API payloads as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or MCP bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text.
Add provenance tags to all OpenMetadata outputs before Langflow consumes them.
Restrict Langflow flows to allowlisted nodes only.
requires-engineering: insert a sanitizer/validator between OpenMetadata and Langflow.
requires-engineering: separate the agents onto isolated workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow explicitly handles uploaded files, server filesystem data, and per-flow credentials, and it has broad network egress. OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge, and can emit data through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Together, default workflows can move sensitive metadata from shared storage into outbound requests or logs, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata metadata or lineage records are placed into Langflow flows, they can be forwarded to external model providers or HTTP services.
IF both agents share a workspace or server-side store, files and secrets may be readable by both sides.
mitigations: Remove sensitive datasets from shared flow inputs.
Turn off outbound connectors not needed for the workflow.
Store secrets outside Langflow's per-flow store.
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces and service accounts.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and audit logging.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can execute shell commands, install packages, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP tools. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared external resources and server-side state, so concurrent runs can race or overwrite each other. The profiles do not show locking, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, database, or API object, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Langflow shell steps modify artifacts that OpenMetadata also updates, last-write-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use per-agent service accounts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking or transactions.
requires-engineering: disable shell/package steps in shared environments.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents, and OpenMetadata is a data-collaboration/governance system that can surface lineage and trust metadata. If Langflow treats OpenMetadata outputs as authoritative, downstream nodes may act on incorrect metadata without verification. Because the pair can automate multi-step workflows, the blast radius can extend beyond a single task.
conditions: IF Langflow routes OpenMetadata-derived facts into action-taking nodes, errors can propagate automatically.
IF no verification step exists between OpenMetadata outputs and Langflow decisions, false lineage or governance data can be operationalized.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions.
Require schema validation on OpenMetadata outputs.
Mark OpenMetadata fields as untrusted in Langflow.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and cross-checks.
requires-engineering: separate read-only analysis from action flows.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs on the server filesystem. That combination can create retention and subject-rights mismatches if regulated metadata is copied into Langflow artifacts. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal or governance data is copied into Langflow logs, caches, or flow stores, retention obligations may diverge.
IF OpenMetadata subject-rights workflows depend on deletion or export guarantees, Langflow artifacts may retain stale copies.
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in flow inputs.
Set short retention on Langflow artifacts.
Document which system is system-of-record.
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across both systems.
requires-engineering: perform a residency and certification review.
